about: What every SDK's live suite does against a deployed ATLAS API, in this order. It is data so that the SDKs cannot drift into testing different things: a runner fails on a scenario it does not implement, a run fails if it skips one, and a run fails unless every operation the SDK covers was called. The arbiter is the deployed API, never a mock generated from the same contract.

requires.ATLAS_BASE_URL: The address the API is served from, without /v1.
requires.ATLAS_API_KEY: An API key carrying content:read, end-users:manage, ai:use and usage:read.
requires.ATLAS_WEB_URL: The web address people sign in at, where the consent page is.
requires.ATLAS_CLIENT_ID: The client id of an application registered for sign-in on behalf, with ATLAS_REDIRECT_URI among its redirect addresses.
requires.ATLAS_REDIRECT_URI: A loopback address registered on that application, such as http://127.0.0.1:53682/callback. The runner listens there for the consent page's answer.
requires.ATLAS_PASS_ORG_ID: The organisation the consenting person reads content in.
requires.ATLAS_WEBHOOK_CAPTURE_URL: The request log of the public receiver the application's webhook endpoint points at: a webhook.site token API address, https://webhook.site/token/<uuid>/requests.

scenarios.expect: The key's organisation, application and permissions.
listResources returns at least one READY resource, by title - not an empty list. getResource returns that same resource by id, and getResourceDownload a download address and a file name for it.

scenarios.fault: The first linkEndUser response is read and then discarded, as if the connection had dropped after the API answered.
scenarios.expect: The SDK retries once, and both attempts carry one Idempotency-Key. listEndUsers counts exactly one more active link than before. The same key sent with a different body is refused 409 ATLAS-DEV-010, which proves the API recorded the key.
200, carrying an endorsement from a bipolar sub-dimension of the profile and one from a multi-category sub-dimension.
This period's usage, listing the key's own application.
The link made above answers inactive, with a revocation time.

scenarios.interactive: A person signs in at the printed consent address and chooses Allow. The code expires about a minute after that, so the runner exchanges it as soon as it arrives.
scenarios.expect: The code is exchanged for a pass, and the pass reads all three content operations. A refresh rotates it. The refresh token it replaced is then refused 400 ATLAS-DEV-014, and the pass issued before the refresh still reads.

The newest delivery the receiver captured verifies under the endpoint's secret, as of when it arrived, and the same body with one byte changed is refused. A signature proves who signed, not which environment sent it, so the delivery must also have arrived within the last 24 hours and name a resource the key can read in the environment under test.

Calls past the per-subject request rate draw a 429 carrying Retry-After. The SDK waits at least that long, and the same call then succeeds. It runs last because it spends the key's budget for a window.
